summary.headline: Rico Auto Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT fell to negative INR26.3 crore on INR852 crore revenue and INR9.3 crore EBITDA, driven by air freight costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR852 crore and EBITDA was INR9.3 crore, with PAT at negative INR26.3 crore. For H1 FY27, revenue was INR1,607 crore, EBITDA INR46.9 crore and PAT negative INR29.7 crore. Management attributed the weak quarter to West Asia-related shipping disruption that forced air freight on new single-source programs for Toyota and BMW, with air freight cost cited at about INR40 crore. Management said air shipments should end after November 2026 and reiterated an FY27 revenue target of more than INR3,200 crore, while price-increase negotiations with customers are still ongoing.

segments.name: Aluminium casting
segments.commentary: Contributed 89% of Q2 FY27 revenue. Management said aluminium shipments were on time and had no issues during the quarter.

segments.name: Ferrous (iron) casting
segments.commentary: Contributed about 11% of Q2 FY27 revenue. Management said the heavier iron components drove the freight cost problem, and some light iron components are being moved to other suppliers because they are uneconomic on the company's large machines.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of more than INR3,200 crore, driven by ramp-up of ongoing programs and better utilisation of capacity (implies roughly INR1,593 crore in H2 on H1 of INR1,607 crore).
Air freight expected to end after November 2026; shipping patterns expected to normalise from Q3 with a shift from air to sea freight.
Price-increase negotiations: 2 domestic customers closed, 3-4 more targeted by November end, most customers including BMW (Germany and US) targeted by mid-December 2026.
Management expects a big jump in Q4 FY27 and says price increases and premium freight recovery should be concluded by then.
Management expects at least 10% industry growth next year (FY28), per Mr. Kapur's comments on the domestic market.
capex_capacity: Capacity was expanded to machine more parts in-house to cut dependence on air shipments; management said this added manpower and footprint.
Iron components that are light and uneconomic on large machines are being tagged for transfer to other sources.
Focus stated on transmission, hybrid and EV components for bigger parts; no specific capex amounts or commissioning dates were given.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as strong; management said the company outgrew the industry, with Maruti, Hero and Bajaj cited as growing requirements.
Shipping transit time from India to the US rose from about 5-6 weeks to 10-11 weeks, and Europe transit is similar or longer, pushing up freight cost.
Carbide tooling costs, fuel, aluminium, and labour-driven inflation are not fully passed through; increases are being negotiated, and aluminium prices are now easing.
Two domestic customers have agreed to recover part of the air freight or price increases, and one customer has agreed to contribute toward air freight cost.

qa_highlights.question: Mukesh Mody asked about the long-term strategy to mitigate freight and operating cost volatility, noting INR40 crore paid.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR40 crore was a one-time air freight cost to meet BMW and Toyota commitments, with transit times doubled; it expects zero air shipments after November and is seeking customer recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Bhaskara asked about accountability for the poor quarter and repeated freight issues.
qa_highlights.answer: Management apologised, said it was the worst quarter, and blamed new product launches (about 50 launches) and iron-side heavy components; Mr. Verma said a policy will be set to handle such situations earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Kumar asked about the industry outlook over the next 12-18 months.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects commodity prices, especially aluminium, to ease, domestic demand to stay good through Diwali and Q4, and at least 10% growth next year.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Kumar asked about opportunities across PV, CV, hybrid and EV.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is pursuing hybrid and EV work where possible, and continuing ICE, with focus on transmission and larger hybrid/EV components.

risks_watch: Whether air freight truly stops after November 2026 and sea-route transit times normalise from Q3.
Pace of price-increase and freight-recovery closures with customers, especially BMW in Germany and the US, targeted by mid-December.
Q3 and Q4 margin recovery versus the H2 revenue needed to reach the INR3,200 crore target.
Exit of uneconomic light iron components and their effect on revenue and profit.
Shareholder confidence after repeated freight-related losses; a shareholder questioned management credibility and debt levels, which were not answered on the call.
Middle East tensions affecting energy prices, shipping routes and carbide costs.
summary.management_tone: Apologetic and defensive on the quarter, with confident forward statements on freight normalisation and Q4 recovery that rest on unconfirmed customer negotiations. Management was evasive on the debt question and did not give specific quantified guidance for margins.
key_quotes: This is a onetime cost that we had to bear because of the chaos that was created.
From November onwards, you will see that most of the containers start reaching there.
And we are determined to get out of this, a lot of learnings that have happened and a lot of corrections have also taken place and a lot of changes that are also taking place.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Customer price and air-freight recovery
rows.why: Two domestic customers have closed and 3-4 more are targeted by November end, with BMW and most others by mid-December, but these are still negotiations and not yet signed.

rows.label: Air freight ends; shipping normalises
rows.why: Management expects zero air shipments after November 2026 and a shift to sea freight, against a one-time cost of about INR40 crore in Q2; US transit rose from 5-6 weeks to 10-11 weeks.

rows.label: Q4 FY27 earnings jump

tone.note: Management was apologetic and confident on freight normalisation and Q4 recovery, but evasive on the debt question and gave no quantified margin guidance; analysts pressed on accountability, the INR40 crore freight cost, and the credibility of the INR3,200 crore target.
